frames.narration: The app does not send the query text. It sends the hash 8fdad20c and its variables. The guard finds the hash in the stored queries, which means the query was tested at build time, and reads its recorded analysis: depth 4, cost 310.
The cost is within the budget of 500, so the guard passes the query on. An unknown hash, or a query whose cost was above the budget, would have been rejected here, before any service did any work.
The plan has three rounds. The first one asks the users service for all the users. The answer is 20 users, and each carries its key.
In the second round the router puts the 20 user keys in the batcher. The batcher makes one call to the orders service with all 20 keys. Asking one by one would have been 20 calls.

In the third round the 25 orders refer to only 8 different products. The batcher removes the duplicates and asks the products service once for 8 keys, where one call per order would have been 25 calls.

The router spreads the answers back onto the orders and users and returns one response in the shape the app asked for. The query made 3 calls instead of 46 (1 + 20 + 25), and the number of calls would stay at 3 with 1,000 users.
